prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1194; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Responding to a two-vehicle collision in League City, Texas, I found Driver 1 and Driver 2 stopped in the same lane facing each other, with front-end damage to both vehicles. The damage on each vehicle is consistent with a low-speed head-on impact and matches the impact described by Driver 2. Driver 2 stated the collision happened as I have described it, and two independent witnesses gave accounts that agree with Driver 2 on the sequence of events. Photographs taken at the scene show the damage and its position on both vehicles. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain and was evaluated at the scene. The injury reported is consistent with the force of this type of crash. Both witnesses and I observed that Driver 1 was not inside the vehicle when the collision occurred. I found no indication of earlier damage to either vehicle. Records show Driver 1 is the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. No citations were issued at the scene. This narrative is based on the information available at the time of my investigation.
